title: 100-200 item benchmarks rarely resolve a 5-point accuracy gap
summary: Simulation: on a binary-scored benchmark near 70% accuracy, a paired bootstrap 95% CI detects a true 5-point gap in only 13-19% of 100-item comparisons and 20-34% of 200-item ones; at 500 items detection rises to 51-76%. Median CI half-widths are 7.5-11.0 pp at n=100, 5.3-7.8 pp at n=200, and 3.4-4.9 pp at n=500.

statement.text: For two systems scored pass/fail on the same items at about 70% baseline accuracy, a paired bootstrap 95% CI on the accuracy difference has a median half-width of 7.5-11.0 points at 100 items, 5.3-7.8 at 200 and 3.4-4.9 at 500, and excludes zero for a true 5-point gap in only 13-19% (100 items), 20-34% (200) and 51-76% (500) of comparisons; with no true gap it excludes zero in 3.5-5.2% of comparisons.
qualifiers: Ranges span the two simulated dependence settings: a shared-difficulty mixing probability rho of 0.5 and 0.8, which induce an item-level correlation between the arms' correctness of about 0.25 and 0.64 (rho squared); higher item-level correlation narrows the CI.
400 simulated comparisons per cell and 1000 bootstrap resamples; rates carry roughly +/-2-5 points of Monte Carlo error.
doesNotClaim: That any particular real benchmark has these item correlations.
Anything about continuous or partial-credit metrics, or about averaging several seeds per item.
That a non-significant difference proves the systems are equal.

conditions.analysis: paired bootstrap 95% CI on the accuracy difference
conditions.task: comparing two systems or prompts on one shared benchmark

unknowns: Behaviour at baseline accuracies far from 70%
Behaviour with clustered or duplicated items

testedScope.summary: Monte Carlo simulation, stdlib Python, seed 20261014: n in {100, 200, 500}, true gap in {0, 3, 5, 10} points, shared-difficulty mixing probability rho in {0.5, 0.8} (induced item-level correlation about 0.25 / 0.64), 400 comparisons per cell, 1000 bootstrap resamples.

evidence.title: Simulation results table
evidence.description: One row per (items, true gap, correlation): share of comparisons whose paired bootstrap 95% CI excludes zero, and the median CI half-width in points.

comparison.arms: system A vs system B on the same items

limitations: Synthetic items; dependence comes from a simple shared-difficulty mixture whose column `rho` is the mixing probability, not the between-arm correlation (about rho squared).

evidence.title: Simulation script (stdlib Python, fixed seed)
evidence.description: Regenerates results.csv exactly: python3 paired_bootstrap_sim.py > results.csv. Uses only the Python standard library.
evidence.derivation: Per item, each arm independently reuses a shared difficulty draw with probability rho (the mixing probability), otherwise takes its own draw; arm B's threshold is raised by the true gap. Both arms share the draw with probability rho squared, so the item-level correlation of correctness is about rho squared (0.25 / 0.64), not rho.

reusable: Use the half-widths as a quick prior for how small a gap a 100-500 item binary benchmark can resolve before planning a comparison.
stillCheck: Your benchmark's real item-level correlation between arms (it sets the CI width); compare it with about 0.25 / 0.64 here, not with the rho column
Whether your metric is binary per item
sanityChecks: Compute the paired bootstrap CI on your own per-item results instead of reusing these numbers as your result.
